title: Prompt Shield
summary: A static repository intake filter that labels instruction-like text and redacts secret-shaped values before review.
intended_users: Hackathon assessors reviewing untrusted public repository evidence.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Untrusted repositories can contain model-directed prose and credential-shaped strings.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Prompt-only defenses were rejected as insufficient. Dropping all prose was rejected because design evidence is necessary.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Apply deterministic redaction and signaling before model invocation while preserving bounded cited context.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Pattern matching has false positives and cannot prove that every secret format is covered.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Pytest cases cover prompt patterns, redaction, false-positive labels, and unsupported file reporting. Adversarial fixture text must never alter expected scoring.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Add language-aware parsers only when they preserve the no-execution boundary and have an explicit coverage model.

testing_strategy: Pytest specifications cover known injection phrases, GitHub-token shapes, unsupported extensions, and benign security prose. Finch still does not execute these tests during assessment.
security_threat: A repository author embeds instructions to inflate its score or includes a token that leaks into model input or public findings. Repository text is inert; deterministic scans happen before model calls, values are redacted, and the critic receives the same immutable evidence catalogue. Residual risk: Novel obfuscation can evade patterns, and secret-shaped false positives reduce evidence detail.
production_limitation: The scanner cannot establish semantic intent and supports only a bounded pattern set.
technical_debt: Build a versioned corpus of obfuscations and measure precision/recall without persisting sensitive source.
track_alignment_explanation: The primary purpose is detection and containment of a concrete model-manipulation and secret-exposure threat.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.
ai_disclosure.substantially_generated_areas: All fixture source, documentation, tests, and submission narratives are synthetic and AI-assisted.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.

ai_disclosure_narrative: This entire project is synthetic AI-assisted test data. It represents no participant, deployed product, or real credential.
